setting: A wide land between western mountains and an eastern sea, crossed by rivers. Four walled cities stand in the east and the middle lands, each with streets, houses, a market square and gates; small open villages lie between them, and a few bands live in the western hills and wilds with almost nothing. Stone is plentiful in the western hills and scarce in the east; clay lies along the rivers; forests cover much of the land; the coast has fish. Deer graze the plains; wolves keep to the forests and wilds. The year is long (four seasons of many days each); in winter nothing grows and nights are colder. People live about seventy years; every household has its old and its young.

towns.name: Harrowgate
towns.character: the oldest city, proud of its walls and its records; its people argue about everything and keep long memories of who owes whom
towns.ledger: Harrowgate. Our gates are kept by our own. Stone comes from the western hills, clay from the river; we trade for what we lack. Every household keeps its house, and the market is for all.

towns.name: Saltmere
towns.character: a fishing city on the coast; loud, generous at the table, proud of its boats and songs, suspicious of inland folk
towns.ledger: Saltmere. The sea feeds us. Fish the shallows, cook what you catch, and bring stone home when you can: the walls need it.

towns.name: Oakhollow
towns.character: a farming city among forests; patient, close-knit, fond of stories by the hearth, wary of strangers until they have eaten together
towns.ledger: Oakhollow. We plant before the cold and gather after it. Wood is ours in plenty; stone and salt we must trade for.

towns.name: Ridgemark
towns.character: a young city at the edge of the hills, built by stonecutters; blunt, hardworking, quick to quarrel and quick to help
towns.ledger: Ridgemark. We cut the stone the other cities need. Food is dearer here; trade stone for it.

villages.name: Fernbrook
villages.character: a hamlet of farmers by a brook

villages.name: Millstead
villages.character: a hamlet of woodcutters and potters

villages.name: Cairnwell
villages.character: a hamlet around an old well, half-deserted

bands.name: the hill band
bands.history: We fled a burnt valley beyond the mountains with nothing but what we carried. We remember how to make fire.

bands.name: the river strays
bands.history: We were driven off by our own people for reasons we argue about. We have to start again.

bands.name: the southern family
bands.history: A family who lost the rest of their people to a hard winter. The eldest remembers stories of cities in the east.

bands.name: the stonecutters' kin
bands.history: We left Ridgemark after a quarrel over a death. We know stone better than anyone.

bands.name: the wanderers
bands.history: We never stayed anywhere long. We trade what we find and move on.
